LESSON: LISTENING FOR ENJOYMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 2.1: Listening for enjoyment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening for enjoyment, part of Listening and Speaking in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How do people respond to songs? 1. Why do people sing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening for enjoyment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: Imagination and originality as the learner creatively dances in response to music changing

the dancing with a change in rhythm.

• Communication and collaboration: Listening as the learner listens keenly to interesting and child related music on body

parts (sing, play recorded audio, video).

Values:
• Unity is developed as the learner collaborates with others to dance as a group.

• Love is developed as the learner interacts with others in singing and dancing thus becoming closer and appreciating others’

abilities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Health related issues awareness is enhanced as the learner dances and exercises body muscles while appreciating what music

can do to our health.

Link to other Learning Areas: Creative activities as the learner imitates the rhymes and music with actions and movements in

purposive group/ pairs.

Suggested learning resources: Recorded audio, video clip as learner imitates the rhymes and music with actions and

movements.
